old: Very few yachts reach the threshold in any case (a 60m motor yacht is typically 700 to 1,200 GT).

old: The ownership structure is the vehicle that holds the yacht: personal ownership, a company, or something more layered, together with the jurisdiction in which it is established and the VAT treatment that follows from it. It is among the first decisions an owner makes, among the hardest to unwind, and the one most often left too late; settling it early, and around the owner rather than the transaction’s timetable, is among the first things an independent adviser is engaged to ensure.
new: The ownership structure is the legal arrangement under which the yacht is owned: by the owner personally, through a company, or through something more layered, together with the jurisdiction in which it is established and the VAT treatment that follows from it. The right choice depends on the owner’s residence, intended use, financing, succession plans and tax position. It should be settled before the purchase contract is agreed, around the owner rather than the transaction’s timetable, because changing it after completion can have legal, tax and administrative consequences. It is often left too late, and seeing that it is settled in time is among the first things an independent adviser is engaged to do.
